text: Bulgaria is a driving force behind the processes of building connectivity in Europe, said President Iliana Yotova at a forum in Yerevan (04.05.2026 16:37)

Connectivity is not only a strategic choice. It is a guarantee of our shared security – from the economy to defense. Bulgaria is not only an active partner, but also a driving force behind these processes, said President Iliana Yotova during the discussions of the Eighth Summit of the European Political Community, which is taking place in the Armenian capital, Yerevan. This was reported by the press secretariat of the head of state. Nearly 50 heads of state and government are taking part in the forum, held under the motto “Building the Future: Security and Stability in Europe.” The European Political Community aims to promote political dialogue and cooperation to strengthen the security, stability, and prosperity of the European continent.

It is high time that national projects find a place in our shared geographical and economic connectivity. Southeast Europe is a strategic bridge between our continent, Asia, and the Middle East. Times of crisis open up new opportunities, Yotova said, as quoted in the statement. In her remarks, the president emphasized projects related to the energy and transport connectivity of the Old Continent, in which Bulgaria is actively involved.

Global conflicts have taught us the hard way that we must develop our energy independence and diversify our energy sources, Yotova also said, emphasizing that the gas interconnector between Greece and Bulgaria plays a key role in diversification.

The head of state emphasized that Bulgaria was one of the first countries to expand the capacity of its gas storage facilities after the 2022 gas crisis. She highlighted the significance of one of the largest projects—the Vertical Gas Corridor—which will connect Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, and Hungary. The Bulgarian part of the project is nearly completed.

“We are working to expand the infrastructure for renewable energy, especially along the Black Sea coast, as well as with solar systems,” Iliana Iotova also said, as quoted in the press release. She emphasized that Bulgaria is one of the largest and most consistent supporters of clean and safe nuclear energy, while the European Union is only now reconsidering its position on the issue.

The President highlighted the importance of transport connectivity. We insist on accelerating the construction of Corridor 8, which will connect Bulgaria, North Macedonia and Albania – in practice, the Adriatic Sea with the Black Sea. This is not only an important economic project, but also, from a security perspective, not only for the region but for all of Europe, Yotova said. She emphasized that these projects are important for the integration of the countries of the Western Balkans, as they will contribute to bilateral connectivity, as well as to the transport arteries across Europe. The President also called for the development of the Trans-European Transport Network – a large-scale project for building infrastructure for different types of transport in Europe.

Iliana Yotova also emphasized the importance of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor, which will contribute to connectivity between Europe and Asia. The head of state highlighted how important it is to build another bridge over the Danube River and to complete the transport connection between Silistra and Călărași.

In her statement, the president pointed out that Bulgaria has strengthened the role of its Black Sea ports. These are projects important not only for the economy, but also for the security of the continent, Yotova said.

Bulgaria is building industrial zones around major cities to attract investment and ensure the security of regional supply chains. The President highlighted Bulgaria’s strong position in the development of new technologies, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence. Bulgaria is one of the six countries selected by the European Commission for the construction of an artificial intelligence gigafactory.

The head of state also placed emphasis on the importance of the European Union’s Multiannual Financial Framework. It is extremely important for economic projects, regional connectivity and development to preserve the cohesion policy, and Bulgaria will firmly insist on this, Yotova emphasized.

“The Vertical Gas Corridor is of strategic importance for Europe’s energy security. In addition to the economic benefits, it also has political significance at a time of serious geopolitical divisions and military conflicts,” President Iliana Yotova said earlier today.
